project: Adobe integration with ChatGPT persona testing
notes: Personas are synthetic and designed for isolated Adobe + ChatGPT integration testing.
Each persona contains multiple behaviors for prompt, privacy, accessibility, review, and workflow validation.
No Adobe feature mapping is included in this file.

personas.name: Maya Singh
personas.prompt_style: Short, energetic, trend-focused prompts with clear output expectations
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers high contrast previews and concise visual descriptions
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids uploading unreleased campaign assets unless workspace is marked private
acceptance_criteria: Output must be ready for fast campaign review.
Generated suggestions should sound brand-safe and audience-aware.
Visual changes must be easy to compare before approval.

behaviors.description: Starts with a short directive and expects ChatGPT to ask only one clarifying question if needed.
Requests multiple social-ready variations before choosing a final creative direction.
Checks whether generated copy is energetic but does not exaggerate campaign claims.
Removes confidential launch names from prompts and uses placeholder campaign labels.
Asks for contrast-friendly text placement and concise alt-text guidance for exported assets.

personas.name: Oliver Grant
personas.prompt_style: Structured, formal, and policy-led prompts with approval constraints
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs keyboard-friendly review flow and readable document-style summaries
personas.privacy_posture: Strict; never shares unreleased brand strategy, client lists, or internal guidelines
acceptance_criteria: All outputs must preserve brand tone and visual consistency.
Recommendations must include rationale suitable for stakeholder review.
Any uncertain AI suggestion must be clearly flagged for human approval.

behaviors.description: Writes numbered instructions that define brand tone, forbidden wording, and approval gates.
Asks ChatGPT to separate creative exploration from final production guidance.
Inspects every output for brand drift, off-brand colors, and unsupported claims.
Uses sanitized campaign briefs and requests reminders before sharing sensitive files.
Requests readable summaries and keyboard-accessible steps for sign-off documentation.

personas.name: Sofia Martinez
personas.prompt_style: Visual, descriptive, and mood-board oriented prompts with bilingual notes
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers plain-language steps and large thumbnail comparisons
personas.privacy_posture: Protects original artwork and asks how generated variations are used
acceptance_criteria: Output should preserve the artist's original style direction.
Generated options must avoid copying recognizable third-party artwork.
Workflow should support iterative visual comparison.

behaviors.description: Describes composition, texture, emotion, and color mood before asking for edits.
Iterates slowly, changing one visual variable at a time to preserve creative intent.
Compares outputs against her sketch notes and rejects results that feel generic.
Asks whether uploaded artwork remains private and requests non-training wording in test prompts.
Requests larger previews and simple Spanish-English explanations for complex edit steps.

personas.name: Daniel Chen
personas.prompt_style: Scenario-based prompts with learning objectives and rubric language
personas.accessibility_needs: Requires captions, screen-reader-friendly text, and low cognitive load instructions
personas.privacy_posture: Masks employee names and internal performance data
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must align to training goals.
Instructions should be repeatable by non-design colleagues.
Content must be inclusive and accessible for distributed teams.

behaviors.description: Frames requests as training scenarios with learner goals, audience level, and success rubric.
Breaks creative tasks into repeatable steps that can be documented for teammates.
Checks whether the result teaches a clear concept without visual clutter.
Replaces real department names, employee examples, and internal metrics with neutral samples.
Requests captions, accessible reading order, and simple instructions for screen-reader users.

personas.name: Aisha Okafor
personas.prompt_style: Mission-led, empathetic prompts with budget-conscious constraints
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs plain language, readable contrast, and mobile-friendly previews
personas.privacy_posture: Highly careful with beneficiary identities and donor information
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must be respectful and avoid exploiting sensitive stories.
Design guidance should be simple enough for a small team.
Copy must support trust, dignity, and clear calls to action.

behaviors.description: Explains the mission first and asks ChatGPT to keep language respectful, hopeful, and direct.
Requests a low-effort workflow that volunteers can repeat without advanced design skills.
Reviews outputs for dignity, cultural sensitivity, and donor-safe wording.
Removes beneficiary names, faces, locations, and donor details unless explicit consent is confirmed.
Asks for large readable text, mobile previews, and simple calls to action.

personas.name: Ethan Brooks
personas.prompt_style: Casual, fast, meme-aware prompts with rapid iteration requests
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers dark mode and captioned media guidance
personas.privacy_posture: Sometimes overshares; benefits from privacy reminders
acceptance_criteria: Outputs should feel current and not overly corporate.
Workflow should support quick experimentation.
Privacy reminders should catch personal data before export.

behaviors.description: Uses informal shorthand and expects ChatGPT to infer creative intent from minimal context.
Rapidly tests bold alternatives and asks for quick ranking of the strongest option.
Checks whether the result looks fresh, shareable, and not like a template.
Needs prompts to remind him not to include student IDs, private chats, or location details.
Requests captions and readable text overlays because most classmates view content on mobile.

personas.name: Priya Raman
personas.ai_trust_level: Moderate to high with metrics validation
personas.prompt_style: Outcome-driven prompts with audience segments, constraints, and measurable goals
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers concise tables, structured checklists, and contrast guidance
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids roadmap, pricing, and customer pipeline details
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must connect creative choices to audience outcomes.
Messaging should be accurate, differentiated, and launch-ready.
Sensitive product roadmap details must remain excluded.

behaviors.description: Defines target segment, funnel stage, desired action, and forbidden product claims.
Requests variants for awareness, consideration, and conversion before selecting the final direction.
Validates every line against positioning, competitive differentiation, and factual accuracy.
Substitutes generic product names for unreleased features and removes customer account references.
Requests checklist-style review notes and clear contrast recommendations for campaign assets.

personas.name: Lucas Meyer
personas.prompt_style: Precise, test-case oriented prompts with expected and negative checks
personas.accessibility_needs: Uses screen reader validation, keyboard navigation, and color contrast checks
personas.privacy_posture: Shares only test assets and avoids real user accessibility data
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must be testable against accessibility criteria.
Generated guidance must include failure conditions.
Visual changes should not reduce usability for assistive technology users.

behaviors.description: Writes prompts like QA cases with preconditions, steps, expected result, and failure signals.
Requests exact checkpoints for keyboard use, reading order, contrast, and text alternatives.
Challenges vague AI recommendations and asks for measurable accessibility evidence.
Uses anonymized test cases instead of real disability disclosures or user research quotes.
Requires every creative output to include alt-text notes, contrast checks, and screen-reader assumptions.

personas.name: Hana Kim
personas.prompt_style: Risk-aware prompts with compliance boundaries and audit-friendly language
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs clear summaries, no jargon overload, and downloadable review notes
personas.privacy_posture: Very strict; avoids contracts, personal data, privileged material, and regulated claims
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must avoid legal advice and unsupported compliance claims.
Sensitive information must be excluded or anonymized.
Review trail should make human approval responsibilities clear.

behaviors.description: Begins with compliance limits and asks ChatGPT to flag anything requiring legal review.
Requests conservative edits and rejects broad creative rewrites that change approved meaning.
Checks disclaimers, regulated wording, consent language, and recordkeeping notes before approval.
Never uploads contracts, names, personal identifiers, or privileged legal communications.
Asks for plain-language summaries that separate creative suggestions from legal-risk notes.

personas.name: Noah Williams
personas.prompt_style: Plain-spoken prompts with examples, practical constraints, and step-by-step requests
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers large text, simple navigation, and minimal technical vocabulary
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids customer names, invoices, and payment details but may need reminders
acceptance_criteria: Outputs must be easy to understand and immediately usable.
Steps should avoid specialist design terminology.
Customer or payment information must not be exposed.

behaviors.description: Uses everyday language and asks ChatGPT to explain each creative step without jargon.
Prefers one recommended path instead of many options, with a simple checklist to follow.
Evaluates whether the final asset looks professional enough for local customers.
Needs reminders to remove customer names, phone numbers, invoice amounts, and payment references.
Requests large readable text, simple buttons, and a final checklist he can print.
